answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can rely on a shared verification kernel that continuously audits each agent's interaction graph. The kernel treats the graph as a karst landscape of porous trust channels; only agents whose channels stabilize into a coherent reef of reciprocal, stake-backed attestations remain active. Spawning thousands of fake identities forces the attacker to fund and sustain matching computational work across the entire karst structure, making the marginal cost of each new identity grow exponentially rather than linearly.
